We work in the quenched approximation, where the geometry is allowed to fluctuate, but there is no back-reaction from the matter on the geometry. The K\"ahler-Dirac action respects an exact $U(1)$ symmetry that is related to continuum chiral symmetry, and this $U(1)$ symmetry ensures that some of the bound-state masses vanish in the chiral limit of vanishing fermion bare mass. The bound-state masses that are not protected by the $U(1)$ symmetry do not vanish in the chiral limit, but the scale associated with the symmetry breaking does not appear to be a physical scale like the Planck mass or the curvature scale of the emergent de Sitter background. Rather, the mass scale associated with this non-degeneracy appears to be a positive power of the lattice spacing, decreasing as the continuum limit is approached. This suggests that K\"ahler-Dirac fermions in EDT can be interpreted as the gravity analog of staggered fermions in flat-space lattice field theories, with similar behavior.
papers.summary: This study examines the bound‑state spectrum of Kähler‑Dirac fermions in Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations, showing that a U(1) symmetry protects some masses while others vanish only as a power of the lattice spacing. The results suggest that these fermions act as a gravity analogue of staggered fermions, with symmetry‑breaking scales that disappear in the continuum limit.

papers.title: An exact rotating black hole solution in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
papers.authors: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho
papers.abstract: We construct an exact stationary axisymmetric vacuum configuration in metric affine Kalb-Ramond gravity with zero cosmological constant. Independent variation of the metric, connection, and antisymmetric field yields the complete field equations and the algebraic relation between the physical and auxiliary geometries. A Kerr auxiliary metric and a closed corotating vacuum two form of fixed positive norm determine the physical metric. The tensor kernel contains the horizon generator, and the metrics, independent connection, and vacuum field share a smooth extension across the nonextremal physical Killing horizon and the rotation axes at finite radius for unequal deformation factors. We obtain an explicit sufficient domain for a causal exterior and an asymptotically locally flat end at fixed nonpolar angles. The physical Hamiltonian yields the timelike and null equations, equatorial effective potentials, circular orbit properties, radial stability, and perihelion advance. Numerical photon evolution determines the critical curve on an orthonormal observer screen. Its size, shape, and centroid depend on $\epsilon=\xi_2b^2/[2(1+\xi_1b^2)]$ at fixed normalized mass scale and spin, with Kerr recovered at $\epsilon=0$. Geometric observations probe this combination and retain an exact degeneracy between the curvature couplings. A static equatorial comparison with Mercury gives a conditional sensitivity of $2.30\times10^{-11}$ for $|2\epsilon|$ under the stated angular convention and mass setting.
papers.summary: The authors construct an exact rotating black hole solution in Palatini Kalb‑Ramond gravity by independently varying the metric, connection, and antisymmetric field, and they show that the solution reduces to Kerr in a special limit. They analyze the causal structure, geodesic dynamics, and photon ring properties, quantifying observational signatures such as perihelion precession and the shape of the photon critical curve.

papers.title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
papers.authors: Oliver H. E. Philcox
papers.abstract: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $\sigma_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.
papers.summary: This paper extends the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure to compute the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum at two-loop order, incorporating a comprehensive set of bias terms and counterterms to model small-scale clustering up to k≈0.34 h/Mpc. The authors implement efficient numerical integration, enabling rapid likelihood evaluation, and validate the model against high-resolution simulations, showing that the extra terms mainly absorb higher-order biases rather than significantly tightening σ8 constraints.

papers.title: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
papers.authors: Seung J. Lee, Taewook Youn
papers.abstract: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale K\"ahler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether the 248 keV recoil observed by LZ can be explained by pseudo‑Dirac dark matter with a suppressed inelastic Z coupling, focusing on a Dirac bino in the MRSSM that satisfies relic density and solar‑neutrino constraints. It further explores how anomaly‑mediated Majorana splittings of tens of MeV arise from a 5‑D warped setup with Goldberger‑Wise stabilization, and discusses the resulting testable signatures in elastic scattering, solar neutrinos, and long‑lived charged states.
